title: Neuropsychological and Emotional-Behavioral Profiles in Pediatric Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: A Single-Center Clinical Study
content: Background: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked disorder caused by out-of-frame variants in the DMD gene, resulting in dystrophin deficiency and progressive muscle degeneration. Beyond motor involvement, evidence links DMD to cognitive impairment and emotional-behavioral (EB) burden, potentially related to altered expression of brain dystrophin isoforms (Dp71, Dp140, Dp427). Objectives: To characterize the neuropsychological and EB profile of a pediatric cohort of children with DMD and to investigate potential genotype–phenotype associations. Methods: This monocentric, cross-sectional study, included 21 children with DMD. Neuropsychiatric comorbidities were assessed using a multimodal psychometric battery. Cognitive, neurodevelopmental and genetic data were also collected and analyzed. Results: In the cohort, 6/20 children (30%) showed autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related features and 7/20 (35%) demonstrated attentional difficulties on at least one screening measure, with both rates exceeding those reported in the general pediatric population. Internalizing symptomatology was the prevalent EB domain of difficulty. Emotional dysregulation (ED) emerged as a distinct area of vulnerability and significantly predicted broader psychopathological involvement (p=0.004–0.029). Among the 11 children who underwent cognitive assessment, 5 (45.5%) had a Full-Scale Intelligence Quotient (FSIQ) <85. The Dp140−/Dp71+ genotype was significantly associated with poorer cognitive functioning (FSIQ<85, p = 0.048), with a trend toward increased vulnerability to ASD-related features (p = 0.099). Conclusions: Children affected by DMD showed heterogeneous neurocognitive and EB profiles, with ED consistently associated with broader psychopathology. Cognitive vulnerability was associated with specific dystrophin isoform expression pattern. These findings argue for standardized neuropsychiatric screening from diagnosis to guide personalized intervention.
